label: End of long sequences starting with e: the <DEL> step or a late p input (rare, conjunctive)
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.006% of steps). It fires only at the end of the original phase or on the <DEL> step (t = 6..9, mostly L = 8-9) and never in the copy phase. Nearly all activation (82% of mass) is in sequences whose first token is e. About half the mass is on <DEL> and about a third is on an input p late in the original phase (orig_idx 6-8). It is stronger when the prefix holds several digits, especially repeated 1s. The top example (4.5) is e a k 1 1 u x p 3. The predicate (<DEL> or late p, in sequences starting with e) covers about 62% of active steps and 67% of mass, but precision is only about 1%: most sequences starting with e never activate it. Requiring two or more 1s raises precision to about 14% but loses most recall. So these conditions are necessary context, not sufficient. It does not fire on early steps (t < 6), short sequences (L <= 5), or copy-phase outputs.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=e (+5.48), orig3=1 (+3.19), orig1=a (+2.92), orig4=1 (+2.77), prev_tok=x (+2.44), phase=0 & in_tok=p (+2.44). Lower it: phase=2 (-3.44), next_out=- (-2.52), t=3 (-1.87), prev3_tok=- (-1.60).
